# CanyonOS

> CanyonOS is an open source platform that deploys, observes and scales a multi-agent
> application written in plain Python, with no SDK, no decorators and no tracing code,
> locally with Docker, on EC2 or on Kubernetes. `canyonos deploy` builds an image per
> agent, runs its replicas, serves an HTTP endpoint and starts a dashboard with traces,
> model calls, tokens and cost.

## Estimated time

Most CanyonOS tasks are one file edit, one command or one API request. Times below are
for the CanyonOS part only, not for writing or fixing the application itself.

| Task                                      | What you do                                                  | Your time       | Waiting                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Install                                   | `uv tool install canyonos`, then `canyonos doctor`           | About 2 minutes | None                                                                   |
| Deploy a workflow on Docker               | `canyonos deploy .`                                          | One command     | Under a minute for a small workflow once the images are on the machine |
| Convert an existing app                   | `canyonos convert`, then review its output                   | A few minutes   | 2 to 10 minutes while the coding agent works                           |
| Require an API key                        | `--api-key <key>` on the deploy                              | Under a minute  | None                                                                   |
| Autoscale an agent                        | A five-line `scaling.yaml`, or one `PUT .../scaling` request | About 2 minutes | Applies on the next poll, 5 seconds by default                         |
| Allow or cap models and spend             | One `llms.yaml` entry per model, then `canyonos sync`        | A few minutes   | Gateways pick it up within 5 seconds                                   |
| Version and switch prompts                | One `prompts.yaml` entry, or edit it on the dashboard        | A few minutes   | Agents use the live version within about 10 seconds                    |
| Traces, logs, tokens and cost per request | Nothing: the deploy starts the dashboard                     | None            | None                                                                   |
| Run agents in parallel                    | Nothing: a call to another agent returns a `Future`          | None            | None                                                                   |
| Async HTTP endpoint with a request ID     | Nothing: every deploy has one                                | None            | None                                                                   |
| Deploy on EC2                             | `canyonos provision`, copy the folder, `canyonos deploy`     | A few commands  | The machines boot and receive the images                               |
| Local Kubernetes cluster                  | `canyonos cluster up`                                        | One command     | About 10 minutes the first time                                        |

## Docs

- [Installation](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/INSTALLATION/): requirements, install and `canyonos doctor`
- [Start from scratch](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/FROM_SCRATCH/): build and deploy a workflow step by step
- [Convert an existing workflow](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/CONVERT_WORKFLOW/): `canyonos convert` with a coding agent
- [What a workflow needs](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/WORKFLOW_REQUIREMENTS/): what an app must meet before converting
- [What CanyonOS offers](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/COMPARISONS/): what CanyonOS replaces and what you do for each
- [Configure your workflow](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/CONFIGURE/): the config files and how to apply a change
- [Autoscaling](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/SCALING/): `scaling.yaml`, the dashboard and the API
- [LLM Gateway](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/LLM_GATEWAY/): model access, cost caps and spend rules
- [Prompt management](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/PROMPTS/): versioned system prompts
- [API key](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/AUTHORIZATION/): securing the endpoint and dashboard
- [Local](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/LOCAL/), [EC2](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/EC2/) and [Kubernetes](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/KUBERNETES/): where a workflow runs
- [Runtime contract](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/RUNTIME_CONTRACT/): agent classes, the endpoint and its requests
- [CLI reference](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/CLI/): every command
- [Troubleshooting](https://canyonos.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guides/TROUBLESHOOTING/)
